course.title: AngularJS — Legacy Maintenance, Testing and Modernization
course.description: A visual-first, practical AngularJS 1.x course for reading, maintaining, testing, securing and planning the modernization of existing applications. AngularJS is end-of-support software and is not recommended here as a starting point for new production projects.
course.version_scope: AngularJS 1.x; reference documentation snapshot for 1.8.4 checked 2026-10-15. The framework reached end of support in January 2022. Confirm the deployed version before applying examples.
prerequisites: JavaScript variables, functions, objects, arrays and browser events.
Basic DOM manipulation and browser developer tools.
JSON and HTTP knowledge is helpful for intermediate material.
course.learning_window: Approximately 8–12 weeks depending on prior JavaScript experience and project depth.
learning_outcomes: Explain AngularJS 1.x architecture, lifecycle, modules, scopes, directives, services and digest behavior.
Build and inspect data-bound views, forms, components and route-driven single-page flows.
Integrate REST APIs using services, promises and explicit loading/error states.
Write and debug unit/integration tests for existing AngularJS features.
Review security, accessibility, dependency, performance and deployment risks in an unsupported codebase.
Produce a practical maintenance or incremental modernization plan with rollback and feature-parity criteria.
course.legacy_warning: AngularJS reached end of support in January 2022. Use this material for maintenance, audit, migration and historical understanding; prefer a currently supported framework for greenfield applications.
